plan: [ This is a 3-bidder, independent private values, second-price auction. With no informative history and one round, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding 15 ensures I win whenever the competitors’ top bid is below 15 and pay only the second-highest bid; if their top bid exceeds 15, I lose and pay nothing. No benefit from shading or overbidding. Use allowed $0.1 increments; 15.0 is valid. ]

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Underbidding risks losing positive-profit wins; overbidding risks winning when the second-highest bid exceeds your value (yielding negative profit). With values redrawn each round and no history to exploit, there’s no strategic benefit to deviation. To maximize expected profit this round, I will bid exactly my value, $36.0. Ties are random; truthful bidding avoids downside from overbidding while capturing all profitable wins. ]

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. It maximizes expected profit by ensuring you win exactly when your value exceeds competitors’ highest bids and pay the second-highest bid if you win. With no informative history and uniform values 0–49, deviating (overbidding risks negative payoff; underbidding risks losing profitable wins) reduces expected profit. Therefore, bid exactly $42.0. ]
